title: Good Leaders Are Contrarian
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Admired Leadership redefines the contrarian leader. The post says contrarians are not people who oppose everyone else or disagree for its own sake; they live in the future while others focus on the present. Citing Panera founder Ron Shaich, it describes thinking future back, staking out positions based on what will matter tomorrow. Contrarians still listen, collaborate and weigh multiple views, but they begin analysis from a different starting point. The author warns that reflexive rejection of others' views is merely disagreeableness, and concludes that the best leaders see where things are going faster by working backward from the future.
points: True contrarian leaders are not opposite for its own sake; they orient to the future rather than the present.
Shaich's future-back thinking means staking positions on what will matter tomorrow.
Contrarians challenge assumptions most when conventional wisdom is most confident.
Reflexively dismissing others' views is disagreeableness, not contrarianism.
Contrarians still listen and collaborate; what differs is the starting place of their analysis.
quotes: True contrarians do not try to do the opposite of what everyone else is doing, nor do they take a contrary stand just to be different.
They stake out a position or view based upon what they see happening in the future, not upon what they believe the contemporary thinking suggests is happening now.
The more the conventional wisdom suggests the “correct” path forward, the more such leaders are likely to suggest that thinking differently could pay big dividends.
Leaders who immediately reject or denigrate the views of others are not being contrarian, they are simply being disagreeable.

Contrarian leaders listen, collaborate, and consider multiple viewpoints before making judgments and decisions, just like everyone else. But as contrarians, they begin their analysis from a different starting place.
They are faster than others in seeing where things are going because they work backward from the future.
